rendered.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color Ally deck built around airbend, earthbend, firebend, and waterbend triggers that draw cards and eventually transform him into a board-wiping, life-gaining threat. Infinite loops exist too: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] together with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] make infinite creature ETBs and tokens for a single mana once assembled.

strategy: Ramp early with mana dorks and land tutors to hit [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Trigger all four bending types in a turn with [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] to transform him into the game-ending back face.
Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] for infinite tokens.
Use Lesson spells to fuel [[Gran-Gran]], [[Uncle Iroh]], and [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] for cheap card advantage and earthbend counters.
Lean on Shrines like [[Sanctum of Calm Waters]] and [[The Spirit Oasis]] to keep drawing extra cards each turn.

keep: A hand with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and cheap mana sets up the combo line.
sendBack: Five-color hands without fixing from [[Chromatic Lantern]] are too clunky to keep.
A hand with no early plays and only one color source struggles to cast Lessons.

tips.text: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] airbends a permanent, then [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] creates a token when you cast it from exile.
[[Monk Gyatso]] lets you airbend a targeted creature, dodging removal while [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] rewards recasting it.
[[Wan Shi Tong, Librarian]] grows and draws cards whenever an opponent's tutor, such as [[Mystical Tutor]] effects, triggers.

rendered.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifact counters deck where tapping Kilo and other permanents triggers proliferate, snowballing counters across artifacts and planeswalkers. The deck assembles multiple infinite combos such as [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana, or [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns, while grinding value from proliferate synergies like [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] and [[Contagion Engine]].

strategy: Ramp early with artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3.
Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] repeatedly to proliferate counters, growing artifacts and planeswalkers each turn.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana to fuel the board.
Use [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] to take infinite extra turns.
Backup draw engines like [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] and [[Insight Engine]] refill the hand while counters accumulate.

keep: A hand with [[Basalt Monolith]] and early mana sets up the combo engine fast.
[[Sol Ring]] into a cheap artifact engine piece starts the plan early.
sendBack: A hand missing blue or red sources struggles to cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]].

tips.text: Proliferate from [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] can push charge counters on [[Magistrate's Scepter]] toward an extra turn.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles any proliferate from [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] for faster counter growth.
[[Pemmin's Aura]] can untap [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] repeatedly to trigger its tapped draw ability.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever tapped, driving counters.
Combos with Zirda for infinite mana.
Reduces activation costs, enables mana combo.
Draws and discards when blue creatures tap.
Doubles every proliferate trigger in the deck.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and has no answer if opponents bring artifact hate such as Vandalblast.
Moderate: Removing [[Basalt Monolith]] before it combos with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] stops the infinite mana line.

rendered.overview: [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] leads a Colorless deck built around casting huge colorless spells that get cascade twice, chaining into more free spells as ramp artifacts and Eldrazi fill the board. Alongside that plan, [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana at no cost, feeding activated abilities and X spells for a kill.

strategy: Ramp hard with artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Basalt Monolith]] to reach [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] and follow with mana value 7 or more colorless spells to trigger double cascade.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] to generate infinite colorless mana for activations.
Use [[Eye of Ugin]] and [[Karn, Scion of Urza]] to find or build toward Eldrazi finishers.
Close games with Annihilator attackers or [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] sweeping the board and refilling your hand.

keep: Early ramp like [[Sol Ring]] into a cheap engine piece starts the plan.
A hand with [[Basalt Monolith]] and a path to more mana is worth keeping.
sendBack: Too many colorless-light draws with no ramp piece struggles to reach turn 5.
Hands flooded with lands but no [[Thought-Knot Seer]] or similar threat sit idle.

tips.text: [[Thought-Knot Seer]] strips a key card before you commit [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] to the board.
[[Basalt Monolith]] untaps for {3} and with [[Forsaken Monument]] doubling colorless mana, the loop becomes free and infinite.
[[Karn, Scion of Urza]] can dig for [[Eye of Ugin]] to tutor a late colorless creature.

keyCards.job: Grants double cascade to big colorless spells.
Doubles colorless mana and pumps colorless creatures.
Finds a colorless creature and cheapens Eldrazi spells.
Refills your hand and counters spells late game.
Digs through the library for a needed piece.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Basalt Monolith]] with no answer to an opposing artifact wipe such as a hypothetical Vandalblast effect.
Moderate: Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed, so a fast combo like one built around [[Basalt Monolith]] elsewhere can resolve before you answer it.
Minor: Disrupting [[Basalt Monolith]] before it links with [[Forsaken Monument]] stops the infinite mana line outright.

rendered.overview: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] leads a Naya Dinosaur deck that ramps toward an expensive commander and converts its combat damage into free Dinosaurs cascading onto the battlefield, while pieces like [[Polyraptor]] and [[Forerunner of the Empire]] can spiral into endless tokens and damage once assembled.

strategy: Ramp through early mana sources to reach [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7.
Protect and attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to flip Dinosaurs straight from the library.
Deploy enrage and support Dinosaurs like [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to multiply bodies and damage.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] for endless tokens and damage triggers.
Close games with trampling attackers backed by [[Thrasta, Tempest's Roar]] or [[The Tarrasque]].

keep: [[Sol Ring]] alongside another ramp piece sets up an early curve.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] with a Dinosaur payoff in hand is worth keeping.
sendBack: A hand heavy in one color without fixing for Naya struggles to cast spells.
Too few lands or too many stalls out any plan involving [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]].

tips.text: Deal damage to [[Polyraptor]] with [[Walking Ballista]] to create a token copy via its Enrage ability.
Damage from [[Bellowing Aegisaur]]'s Enrage puts counters on every other creature you control, including [[Walking Ballista]].
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] deals damage to entering Dinosaurs, which can trigger [[Polyraptor]]'s Enrage repeatedly.

keyCards.job: Attacks to put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield free.
Copies itself whenever dealt damage.
Finds a Dinosaur and pings entering Dinosaurs.
Spreads counters across your board when damaged.
Removes threats and feeds counters into combos.
Pings entering creatures, enabling Polyraptor loops.
Provides mana sink removal and board presence.

weaknesses: Moderate: Only [[Thrashing Brontodon]] and [[Zacama, Primal Calamity]] answer problem artifacts or enchantments like [[Null Rod]].
Moderate: With 7 interaction cards, 0 at instant speed and only 1 costing two or less, the deck is slow to answer a fast combo.
Moderate: Without [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] connecting, the deck loses its main way to cheat Dinosaurs into play.

rendered.overview: [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] leads a mono-Red Goblin tribal deck that floods the board with 1/1 Goblin tokens and converts them into damage through sacrifice outlets, haste enablers, and direct burn. The deck assembles [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite commander casts and infinite hasty tokens, otherwise it just overwhelms opponents with wide attacks and burn spells.

strategy: Ramp with [[Sol Ring]], [[Arcane Signet]], or [[Mind Stone]] to cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4.
Activate [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] to double your Goblins into an army of 1/1 tokens each turn.
Assemble [[Skirk Prospector]] with [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] and [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for infinite hasty tokens.
Use sacrifice outlets like [[Tar Pitcher]] and [[Goblin Bombardment]] to turn excess tokens into direct damage.
Finish with burn spells such as [[Fireball]] or [[Goblin War Strike]] once the board is wide.

keep: [[Skirk Prospector]] in hand supports the infinite combo once it comes together.
Early ramp like [[Sol Ring]] into a Goblin payoff starts the plan on time.
sendBack: A hand lacking cheap Goblins and no Red sources struggles to curve out.
Hands with no way to make tokens stall without a path to [[Krenko, Mob Boss]].

tips.text: [[Goblin Lookout]] can sacrifice a token to pump the team right before attacking with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]]'s army.
[[Skirk Prospector]] sacrifices Goblins for mana, feeding [[Goblin Warchief]]'s cost reduction on more Goblin spells.
[[Tar Pitcher]] sacrifices a Goblin to deal 2 damage, cleaning up blockers before swinging with tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]].

rendered.overview: This Jeskai deck leads with the partner gods [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]], attacking with Gods to pile experience counters, then spreading those counters onto creatures while proliferate effects double them again and again. [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] converts stored experience into card draw and direct damage, while a wide package of proliferate and counter-doubling pieces like [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] keep the counters snowballing until combat closes the game.

strategy: Ramp early with [[Sol Ring]] and [[Smothering Tithe]] to reach the commanders around turn 4.
Attack with Gods to trigger [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], gaining experience counters and growing a chosen creature each end step.
Proliferate with [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] to multiply experience and +1/+1 counters across the board.
Activate [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to draw cards equal to stored experience counters and burn opponents for 2 each use.
Use [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] to add an extra counter whenever one would be placed, accelerating the whole plan.

keep: [[Smothering Tithe]] with early mana ramps the plan toward the commanders quickly.
[[The Locust God]] alongside a few lands sets up a steady draw engine.
sendBack: Hands missing blue, red, or white sources can't reliably cast [[Jeska's Will]].
A slow hand with no early plays stalls before [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] can attack.

tips.text: [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] combine so every proliferate places an extra counter on top of the usual one.
[[Tezzeret's Gambit]] draws two cards and proliferates, triggering [[The Locust God]] twice for extra Insect tokens.
[[Teferi's Ageless Insight]] doubles the extra cards from [[Tezzeret's Gambit]], flooding the hand with replacement draws.

keyCards.job: Converts experience counters into cards and opponent damage.
Doubles up counters placed on creatures or yourself.
Turns every card drawn into a flying hasty token.
Proliferates on every spell cast to grow counters.
Doubles extra card draws beyond the first each turn.

weaknesses: Critical: Removing or taxing [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] stops experience gain, counter growth, and the draw engine outright.
Moderate: With only 3 instant-speed answers and a single mass removal spell like [[Blasphemous Act]], a fast board can outrace this deck.
Moderate: The plan leans on combat damage from grown creatures, so a fog effect like [[Ghostly Prison]] from an opponent can stall it out.

strategy.text: Ramp early with [[Sol Ring]] and [[Smothering Tithe]] to reach the commanders around turn 4.
Attack with Gods to trigger [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], gaining experience counters and growing a chosen creature each end step.
Proliferate with [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] to multiply experience and +1/+1 counters across the board.
Activate [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to draw cards equal to stored experience counters and burn opponents for 2 each use.
Use [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] to add an extra counter whenever one would be placed, accelerating the whole plan.

keep.text: [[Smothering Tithe]] with early mana ramps the plan toward the commanders quickly.
[[The Locust God]] alongside a few lands sets up a steady draw engine.

sendBack.text: Hands missing blue, red, or white sources can't reliably cast [[Jeska's Will]].
A slow hand with no early plays stalls before [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] can attack.

tips.text: [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] combine so every proliferate places an extra counter on top of the usual one.
[[Tezzeret's Gambit]] draws two cards and proliferates, triggering [[The Locust God]] twice for extra Insect tokens.
[[Teferi's Ageless Insight]] doubles the extra cards from [[Tezzeret's Gambit]], flooding the hand with replacement draws.

keyCards.job: Gains experience counters and grows a creature each end step.
Converts experience counters into cards and opponent damage.
Doubles up counters placed on creatures or yourself.
Turns every card drawn into a flying hasty token.
Proliferates on every spell cast to grow counters.
Doubles extra card draws beyond the first each turn.
Generates Treasure mana whenever opponents draw cards.

assessment.line: Beyond [[Chaos Warp]] the deck has little answer for a resolved artifact or enchantment like [[Null Rod]].
With only 3 instant-speed answers and a single mass removal spell like [[Blasphemous Act]], a fast board can outrace this deck.
Removing or taxing [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] stops experience gain, counter growth, and the draw engine outright.
The plan leans on combat damage from grown creatures, so a fog effect like [[Ghostly Prison]] from an opponent can stall it out.
Many tapped dual lands can slow an aggressive curve toward casting [[Jeska's Will]] on time.

rendered.overview: [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] leads a Wizard-tribal tempo deck that casts cheap instants and sorceries while countering opponents' spells, drawing cards and looting along the way. The deck can also assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite triggers, or with [[Ghostly Flicker]] for an infinite loop of enters and leaves the battlefield triggers.

strategy: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 to cut costs on instants and sorceries.
Use cheap counterspells and card draw to control the board while Wizards accumulate value.
Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] to copy it endlessly for triggers.
Alternatively loop [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to flicker permanents infinitely.
Grind opponents down with repeated bounce, counters, and card advantage from Wizards.

keep: [[Sol Ring]] with a Wizard like [[Sea Gate Oracle]] sets up an early curve.
[[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] alongside a counterspell keeps opponents off balance.
sendBack: A hand heavy on colorless spells without blue sources struggles to function.
A hand with no early plays past land drops wastes early turns.

tips.text: Copy [[Sublime Epiphany]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to counter two spells and draw a card at once.
Flicker [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] itself with [[Ghostly Flicker]] to copy another spell on the stack again.
Equip [[Diviner's Wand]] onto [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] so her tap ability also grows her power and gives flying.

keyCards.job: Reduces spell costs and draws off counters.
Copies a spell to enable infinite loops.
Flickers permanents to loop with Naru Meha.
Taps Wizards to draw extra cards.
Bounces a threat and draws at end step.
Cuts spell costs and draws on cast.
Copies a cheap spell when it enters.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck has no answer to an opposing enchantment like a [[Null Rod]] effect shutting down its artifact mana.
Moderate: Without [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] the deck loses its cost reduction and extra card draw engine.
Moderate: The deck lacks a fog or pillowfort effect, so a fast combat deck can race past its counters before [[Vendilion Clique]] stabilizes.

With 17 interaction pieces, 13 at instant speed and 10 costing two or less, [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] backs up quick answers.
Without [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] the deck loses its cost reduction and extra card draw engine.
The deck lacks a fog or pillowfort effect, so a fast combat deck can race past its counters before [[Vendilion Clique]] stabilizes.

As a mono-Blue deck with 35 Islands, [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] faces no color-flexibility weakness.

repairReply.overview: This Dimir deck is built around [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and an army of evasive Ninjas that slip in unblocked, trigger ninjutsu, and burn opponents down from cards revealed off the top of the library while card draw and cheap counterspells keep the plan protected.

strategy.text: Play an unblockable creature like [[Tormented Soul]] or [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] early to set up ninjutsu.
Hold mana to ninjutsu [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] in from the command zone when a creature is unblocked.
Deal combat damage with [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] to reveal cards and drain life equal to their cost.
Chain other Ninjas such as [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] and [[Fallen Shinobi]] for extra draw and value.
Protect the attack with cheap counterspells like [[Spell Pierce]] and [[Dispel]] to push through damage.

keep.text: An unblockable creature with mana to ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] starts strong.
[[Mistblade Shinobi]] with a cheap evasive body sets up early damage triggers.

sendBack.text: A hand of costly spells with no path to an unblockable attacker struggles badly.
A hand missing blue or black sources cannot cast [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] on time.

tips.text: Use [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] as a cheap unblockable body to ninjutsu in [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] for reanimation value.
Bounce an unblocked attacker with [[Walker of Secret Ways]] to reuse its ninjutsu trigger and ninjutsu another threat.
[[Satoru Umezawa]] gives every creature card in hand ninjutsu, letting [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] enter from hand cheaply.
Pair [[Silver-Fur Master]] with other Ninjas to reduce ninjutsu costs and boost their power and toughness.

keyCards.job: Commander drains life off revealed cards on hit.
Gives hand creatures ninjutsu for cheap entries.
Returns a creature from any graveyard on hit.
Finds another Ninja card when it connects.
Lets you cast cards exiled from an opponent's library.
Bounces a blocker to clear the attack lane.
Cuts ninjutsu costs and pumps other Ninjas.
Cheap unblockable body to carry ninjutsu triggers.
